# Platform & tooling

**Rows:** 88% (53: 44 ✅ 5 🟡 4 ❌)

**Area:** [Developer tools](../COVERAGE.md#devtools) · **Issues:** [`area:devtools`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Adevtools)

## How isim implements it

- `isim build` and `isim test` read Xcode projects (`isim/tools/isim-build.py`, `xcodeproj.py`, `isim-test.py`).
- Code compiles with clang / lld and Swift 6.2 (Docker); Swift packages are read with `dump-package`.
- isim has its own storyboard compiler (`ibtool.py`), Core Data model compiler (`momc.py`) and asset-catalog format.
- Devices and `--os` are simulated presets.
- Device builds and signing are blocked ([DISTRIBUTION.md](../DISTRIBUTION.md)).

Tracking domains: URLSession requests to the `NSPrivacyTrackingDomains` of a manifest with `NSPrivacyTracking` fail until tracking is authorized (ATT), like iOS 17 (adapted: `NSURLErrorCannotFindHost`). Tested: test_privacy |
| Share / Action extensions (`NSExtensionContext`, `NSExtensionItem`, `SLComposeServiceViewController`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: `UIActivityViewController` lists the app's own and installed apps' Share (app row) and Action (list) extensions whose `NSExtensionActivationRule` accepts the items (dictionary rules evaluated; predicate strings accepted); the extension is loaded into the host app's process (iOS: its own process) and its view controller presented as a sheet, with one `NSExtensionItem` (content text, `NSItemProvider` attachments for text, URLs, images, data); `completeRequest` / `cancelRequest` return to the host's completion handler with the returned items. Social's compose sheet (Post / Cancel, configuration items, characters remaining). `NSItemProvider` is Swift-only on isim; no Photos/Files share flows. Tested (share) |
| Universal Links / Associated Domains | ✅ | ≤17 | `applinks:` (incl. `*.` wildcards, `?mode=developer`) from archived-expanded-entitlements.xcent, and the domain's apple-app-site-association: details for the app's ID, `components` (`/`, `?` string or per-item, `#`, `exclude`, `caseSensitive`, `percentEncoded`, `substitutionVariables`) or legacy `paths` (`NOT`), first match wins. The AASA comes from `$ISIM_DATA/Library/isim/AASA/<domain>.json`, else Apple's CDN (the domain itself in developer mode), fetched once per process; unreachable (offline) → every path opens the app (logged), no AASA on the server → no links, as on iOS (`ISIM_AASA_FETCH=0` never fetches; the network fetch is unverified). https links opened by other apps or `openurl` go to the claiming app (home screen under `isim boot`; the running app with `isim run`) as `NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb`, others to Safari. | Shell script build phases | ✅ | ≤17 | like Xcode's: run by default in their place among the target's build phases (a script before Compile Sources runs before compiling and its `.swift`/`.m`/`.c` outputs are compiled; scripts before Link Binary / Copy Bundle Resources / Copy Files run there, the rest after the product is assembled; aggregate targets run theirs in order); Xcode's environment (the build settings: `SRCROOT`, `PROJECT_DIR`, `BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR`, `TARGET_BUILD_DIR`, `CONFIGURATION`, `PRODUCT_NAME`, `TARGET_NAME`, `INFOPLIST_PATH`, `EXECUTABLE_NAME`, `CONTENTS_FOLDER_PATH`, `UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH`, `DERIVED_FILE_DIR`, …; `ACTION`, `SCRIPT_INPUT_FILE_n`/`_COUNT`, `SCRIPT_OUTPUT_FILE_n`/`_COUNT`, `.xcfilelist`s as resolved copies in `SCRIPT_INPUT_FILE_LIST_n`/`SCRIPT_OUTPUT_FILE_LIST_n`); dependency analysis: skipped when every output is newer than every input and the phase is unchanged, always run with "Based on dependency analysis" off or without outputs (Xcode's warning), a missing input fails like Xcode; `runOnlyForDeploymentPostprocessing` phases only with `DEPLOYMENT_POSTPROCESSING=YES`; a failing script fails the build (`Command PhaseScriptExecution failed with a nonzero exit code`) after its output. Adapted: scripts run on Linux, so ones calling macOS tools (`xcrun`, `codesign`, `plutil`) fail: `-skip-script-phases` skips every phase (`-run-script-phases`, the old opt-in, is accepted); phases run one at a time; isim rebuilds a target's product each build, so phases whose outputs are inside the product run again. CocoaPods `[CP]` phases are replaced by isim (next rows). Tested (BuildPhases fixture: order, codegen, xcfilelists, environment, skipping, deployment-only, failure; test_toolchain_more) |

Remote `binaryTarget`s: the zip downloaded (https), its SHA-256 checked against the manifest's checksum (what `swift package compute-checksum` prints), extracted into the cache. Not done: package registries (`.package(id:)`), updating existing pins (delete them to re-resolve), credentials other than git's own. Tested without network (git repositories with tags behind `file://` URLs, a transitive dependency, v1 and v2 `Package.resolved`, the artifact from a local HTTPS server, a wrong checksum; test_toolchain_more) |

Audited: the declarations of every 18.x/26.x/27.x row of this file, a clang AST sweep of all Objective-C header declarations and a sweep of all public Swift overlay declarations for well-known iOS 17.5+ API names (added: custom containers, `gesture(_:isEnabled:)`, slider tick builders, `dayOfYear`, `CLServiceSession` and `CLLocationUpdate` diagnostics, StoreKit win-back and `currentEntitlements(for:)`, companion LocalAuthentication policies, `PHPickerFilter.spatialMedia`, `GKAccessPoint` deep links, the Apple Pencil Pro APIs). Tested by compiling 42 Objective-C and 33 Swift uses (tests/ui/test_sdk_availability.py). The versions left unconfirmed by the first audit, checked against Apple's documentation pages (docs/API-SWEEP.md): `AppStore.Platform` and `AppTransaction.originalPlatform` (18.4), `URLRequest.allowsPersistentDNS` (18.0) and `WKWebpagePreferences.UpgradeToHTTPSPolicy` / `preferredHTTPSNavigationPolicy` (18.2, Swift and Objective-C) are annotated; `AppTransaction.appTransactionID` (16.0), `Transaction.appTransactionID` (15.0) and `@Entry` (13.0) need none at iOS 17; `NWError.wifiAware` (26.0) cannot be (Swift has no availability on enum cases with associated values, like Apple's interface). APIs Apple marks unavailable on iOS are too: the macOS / watchOS LocalAuthentication policies (`deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithWatch`, `…BiometricsOrWatch`, `…WristDetection`) and error codes (`biometryNotPaired`, `biometryDisconnected`, `invalidDimensions`).
